title: Bad travel advice from AI: From bogus bars to visa fails
source_used: Vancouver Is Awesome (Bodog roundup distributed by Stacker)
key_facts: The page says the story was produced by Bodog and reviewed and distributed by Stacker; Vancouver Is Awesome carries it.
It collects cases of AI travel advice going wrong.
Two hikers were told by a local guide, a travel agency owner who spoke to the BBC, that the 'Sacred Canyon of Humantay' in Peru does not exist; they had paid an extra $160.

Australian marketing strategist Mark Pollard reportedly was stranded in Mexico City after trusting ChatGPT's visa advice for Chile; Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade publicised the case.
A Singapore traveller said on TikTok that Notion AI planned a day trip to Ba Na Hills from Hanoi, about 1,400 km there and back.
Travel writer Jordan Waller told The Points Guy that ChatGPT suggested a Lisbon venue, Palacio do Mago, which it later conceded it had invented.
Air Canada was ordered to pay compensation after its chatbot wrongly told a customer he was eligible for a bereavement refund.
Airbnb and Expedia now carry disclaimers that machine-generated answers may be wrong; the advice is to check every part of an itinerary independently.
quote_evidence: The only problem was that this particularly apt Lisbon travel tip turned out to be nothing more than a wild ChatGPT hallucination
the number one rule when utilizing an AI travel planner to help plan your trip: Always independently check every aspect of your itinerary.
why_it_matters_hint: Travellers who trust AI itineraries without checking can lose money or be stranded.
event_date: Mixed and mostly undated older cases; roundup carried 13 Oct 2026
notes: Full text read. Branded roundup (the page says produced by Bodog, distributed by Stacker), retelling mostly older and undated cases first reported by the BBC, The Points Guy and others; the entry credits the roundup's producer. Score lowered by 1 as stale/old cases.
